statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-35176 (GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh): REXML before 3.2.7 can be driven into a denial of service by an XML document with many > characters in an attribute value. It is fixed in REXML 3.2.7: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh, https://github.com/ruby/rexml/security/advisories/GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh. Listed the files of every package built from the ruby-3.3 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, on x86_64 and aarch64: the interpreter packages ruby-3.3, ruby-3.3-libs, ruby-3.3-dev, ruby-3.3-doc, ruby-3.3-dbg and ruby-3.3-full, 3.3.10-r0 through the current 3.3.14-r4 (ruby-3.3-libs and ruby-3.3-full 3.3.11-r1 are published for aarch64 only), and the bundled-gem packages ruby3.3-bundler, ruby3.3-debug, ruby3.3-matrix, ruby3.3-minitest, ruby3.3-net-ftp, ruby3.3-net-imap, ruby3.3-net-pop, ruby3.3-net-smtp, ruby3.3-power_assert, ruby3.3-prime, ruby3.3-racc, ruby3.3-rake, ruby3.3-rbs, ruby3.3-rdoc, ruby3.3-rexml, ruby3.3-rss, ruby3.3-test-unit and ruby3.3-typeprof, -r0 through -r4 (ruby3.3-net-imap is 0.4.21-r0 through 0.4.21-r3, 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4). Each bundled-gem package carries its gem's version, not Ruby's (for example ruby3.3-rexml 3.4.4-r0). REXML ships in ruby3.3-rexml: every published build, 3.4.4-r0 through 3.4.4-r4, installs REXML 3.4.4 (usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/specifications/rexml-3.4.4.gemspec), which includes the fix, and no other package installs REXML (ruby3.3-rss contains rss/rexmlparser.rb, RSS's adapter that loads REXML, not a copy of it). ruby3.3-rbs (3.4.0-r0 through 3.4.0-r4) carries usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/gems/rbs-3.4.0/Gemfile.lock, which names REXML 3.2.6: the development lockfile that ships inside the bundled rbs gem and records the gems rbs's own developers locked; it is a text file that neither Ruby nor RubyGems reads when loading gems. Because every published build carries the fix, the range is fixed at the lowest version the owner publishes, 0.1.2-r0 (ruby3.3-net-pop and ruby3.3-prime), so that every published build reads as fixed.

It is fixed in REXML 3.2.7: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh, https://github.com/ruby/rexml/security/advisories/GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh. Each bundled-gem package carries its gem's version, not Ruby's (for example ruby3.3-rexml 3.4.4-r3). REXML ships in ruby3.3-rexml: every published build, 3.4.4-r3 and 3.4.4-r4, installs REXML 3.4.4 (usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/specifications/rexml-3.4.4.gemspec), which includes the fix, and no other package installs REXML (ruby3.3-rss contains rss/rexmlparser.rb, RSS's adapter that loads REXML, not a copy of it). ruby3.3-rbs (3.4.0-r3 and 3.4.0-r4) carries usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/gems/rbs-3.4.0/Gemfile.lock, which names REXML 3.2.6: the development lockfile that ships inside the bundled rbs gem and records the gems rbs's own developers locked; it is a text file that neither Ruby nor RubyGems reads when loading gems. Because every published build carries the fix, the range is fixed at the lowest version the owner publishes, 0.1.2-r3 (ruby3.3-net-pop and ruby3.3-prime), so that every published build reads as fixed.

CVE-2024-35176 (GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh): REXML before 3.2.7 can be driven into a denial of service by an XML document with many > characters in an attribute value. It is fixed in REXML 3.2.7: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh, https://github.com/ruby/rexml/security/advisories/GHSA-vg3r-rm7w-2xgh. Listed the files of every ruby-3.3 and ruby-3.3-dev package published in the DHI Debian 13 repository, on amd64 and arm64: 80 builds, 3.3.11-0 through the current 3.3.14-0. In every build the ruby-3.3 package installs the bundled gem REXML 3.4.4 (usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/specifications/rexml-3.4.4.gemspec), which includes the fix; the ruby-3.3-dev packages contain no REXML files, and no package installs any other REXML version. Every ruby-3.3 package also carries usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/gems/rbs-3.4.0/Gemfile.lock, which names REXML 3.2.6: the development lockfile that ships inside the bundled rbs gem and records the gems rbs's own developers locked; it is a text file that neither Ruby nor RubyGems reads when loading gems. Because every published build carries the fix, the range is fixed at the first published build, 3.3.11-0.
